title: SLA Exception Ledger and Evidence Serialization Guide
summary: Working runbook for recording SLA exceptions for vulnerability remediation and for a compact, SIEM-friendly evidence serialization format. Covers RBAC v2 considerations for evidence access, recommended audit-log fields, export contract for SIEM, and a lightweight ledger schema to track exception approvals and retention.
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a practical ledger format and export contract so remediation teams and the SOC can reliably exchange: (a) SLA exception approvals (when teams request more time to remediate), and (b) the minimal, verifiable evidence payload that travels to our SIEM and long-term evidence store. The goal is to standardize fields, hashes, and access constraints so the RBAC v2 rollout doesn’t break triage or audits.

Scope & constraints:
- Applies to vulnerabilities discovered via scheduled scanners (SCA, container image scans, infra scanners) and external reports that will be tracked in the remediation system.
- Evidence payloads must be compact (avoid full image blobs in SIEM), integrity-protected (sha256), and reference authoritative storage locations (S3, evidence vault).
- SLA exception approvals are recorded in a signed ledger that contains justification, approver, duration, and linking to tickets (Jira/Linear).
- RBAC v2: evidence links in the ledger must resolve only for principals with the `evidence:read` scope; audit logs must capture every access.

Ledger schema (CSV / canonical fields) - minimal required columns:
- ledger_id: human-friendly id (EXC-2026-000123)
- vuln_id: internal vulnerability id (scanner:12345 or CVE-YYYY-NNNN)
- scanner: name of scanner (trivy, snyk, nexus-iq, custom-image-scan)
- detected_at: UTC ISO8601 timestamp when vulnerability first reported
- reported_by: principal id (service account or person)
- requested_by: team or user requesting exception
- sla_deadline: UTC ISO8601 original deadline (if any)
- exception_until: UTC ISO8601 new deadline after approval
- approver: approver id (name/email)
- approver_role: e.g. security-manager, eng-lead, risk-committee
- exception_reason: short free-text reason (max 1024 chars)
- mitigation_controls: comma-separated list (WAF, compensating-config, host-isolation, compensating-script)
- evidence_location: canonical URL (s3://evidence-bucket/2026/EXC-000123/attachment.json)
- evidence_hash: sha256 of the evidence object (hex)
- evidence_format: json | tar.gz | protobuf (we prefer json)
- ticket_refs: comma-separated ticket ids/URLs (JIRA-2345)
- sla_status: pending | approved | revoked | expired
- recorded_by: system account that wrote the ledger (remediation-service@redwood.com)
- recorded_at: UTC ISO8601

Notes on ledger fields and usage:
- ledger_id: generated by remediation-service; deterministic prefix helps search and retention.
- evidence_location must point to the canonical evidence store; SIEM will not store the full blob, only the location and hash.
- evidence_hash is the single source of truth for integrity checks. When evidence is fetched by auditors, they must verify the sha256 before accepting.

Evidence serialization contract (what we send to SIEM):
- For each ledger row, remediation-service emits a compact event to SIEM with the following JSON-compatible flattened fields (SIEM column names in parentheses):
  - event_time (event_time): recorded_at
  - ldap_principal (reported_by): who reported it
  - ledger_id (ledger_id)
  - vuln_identifier (vuln_id)
  - scanner_name (scanner)
  - severity (severity): normalized to critical|high|medium|low|info
  - cvss_score (cvss_score): numeric 0.0-10.0 if available
  - exception_until (exception_until)
  - sla_status (sla_status)
  - approver (approver)
  - evidence_url (evidence_location)
  - evidence_hash_sha256 (evidence_hash)
  - evidence_format (evidence_format)
  - ticket_refs (ticket_refs)
  - assigned_team (assigned_team): from ticket metadata
  - remediation_state (remediation_state): open | in_progress | patched | mitigated | accepted_risk

Design rationales and constraints:
- SIEM ingest must remain lightweight: no binary blobs. The `evidence_url` should be time-bound signed URLs generated per-audit or per-request by the evidence service, not permanent public links.
- RBAC: SIEM roles are read-only; the SIEM will not dereference `evidence_url` without an operator action that obtains a signed URL from remediation-service (this is required to keep direct evidence access auditable).
- Audit logs: each signed URL creation must write an audit event with: user, requester_ip, reason, created_at, ttl_seconds, ledger_id, and evidence_hash. These fields are required for compliance review.

RBAC v2 considerations (practical checklist):
- evidence:read scope required to follow evidence_url. Documented scopes: evidence:read, evidence:list, ledger:read, ledger:write, sla:approve.
- Approvals: only principals in approver_role groups (security-managers, risk-leads) can set sla_status=approved. Enforcement is in remediation-service and enforced by the API gateway.
- Emergency bypass: an emergency token path exists for SRE on-call; all uses create a mandatory `emergency_reason` audit field.

Retention & archival policy (recommended):
- Active ledger rows (any with sla_status != expired and recorded_at within 1 year): keep in primary DB + SIEM index.
- Evidence blobs (full artifacts) retained in evidence-vault for 7 years for high/critical, 3 years for medium, 1 year for low (subject to legal review). SIEM stores only metadata and hashes.
- Ledger CSV exports: snapshot weekly and store with immutable checksum (signed by automation bot).

Operational flows (high level):
1) Scanner finds vuln -> creates vuln ticket and initial remediation row. remediation-service emits SIEM event with remediation_state=open.
2) Owner requests SLA exception via remediation console -> creates ledger draft with evidence_location pointing to staging area.
3) Approver reviews, may request compensating controls -> decision recorded; SLA exception approved -> remediation-service emits SIEM event with sla_status=approved, exception_until populated.
4) Any time evidence blob is accessed (auditor, approver), evidence-service creates signed URL and logs an access audit event. SIEM receives the access-audit event.

Sample SIEM queries (Splunk-like) - quick start:
- Find current SLA exceptions: index=remediation event_type=ledger sla_status=approved | table ledger_id,vuln_identifier,assigned_team,exception_until
- Exceptions expiring in next 72h: index=remediation sla_status=approved | where exception_until < now() + 259200 | table ledger_id,vuln_identifier,approver,assigned_team
- Evidence access spikes (possible exfil): index=remediation event_type=evidence_access | stats count by requester_ip, ldap_principal | sort -count

Ticketing / automation integration notes:
- remediation-service must write ticket_refs back into the ledger row. Ticket systems are the authoritative source for assigned_team and remediation_state.
- Automation bot (rem-bot) signs the weekly ledger export with an internal key and writes a manifest (ledger_export_YYYYMMDD.sig) to the evidence-bucket.

Audit checklist for reviewers:
- Verify ledger row has approver and approver_role populated.
- Confirm evidence_hash verification step exists when fetching artifact.
- Confirm signed URL audit event was generated at time of evidence retrieval.
- Check RBAC group membership for approver matches audit log.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Canonical severity mapping across all scanners (we need a shared normalizer module).
- Exact TTL defaults for signed URLs (30m? 24h?) — current default is 30 minutes, propose increasing to 2 hours for manual audits.
- Integration test for RBAC v2 to validate that SIEM events do not leak evidence URLs to non-privileged roles.

Appendix: example ledger CSV line (single row):
ledger_id,vuln_id,scanner,detected_at,reported_by,requested_by,sla_deadline,exception_until,approver,approver_role,exception_reason,mitigation_controls,evidence_location,evidence_hash,evidence_format,ticket_refs,sla_status,recorded_by,recorded_at

Contact & next steps:
- Primary: Aisha Kumar (aisha@redwood.ai) — own the ledger schema and SIEM contract work.
- Reviewers: Jon Park (SOC), Lena Voss (legal), Marcus Lee (SRE).
- Action items: finalise signed URL TTL (owner: Aisha, due: 2026-02-10), add RBAC test vectors to integration suite (owner: Marcus, due: 2026-02-17), and normalize severity mapping module (owner: Jon, due: 2026-02-24).

Comments / notes to self (informal):
- Keep evidence payloads small — auditors prefer a summary + pointer, not tarballs in the index.
- We should consider a short-lived hash registry endpoint to speed up remote verification without downloading large artifacts.
- Make sure remediation-service rotates the ledger signing key quarterly.

End of working draft.
